past_actions.summary: Host a private dinner with my general managers across all four locations to communicate a long-term vision message: Regional Auto Group is a family institution, not an exit strategy. I am signaling to my leadership team that the business is being built to last, not sold. This reinforces culture, reduces turnover anxiety at the management level, and begins planting the narrative of succession and institutional continuity.

Call an all-hands leadership meeting across all four locations within the next 72 hours. Acknowledge the RoboRide announcement directly — do not let rumors and 'business closing' whispers fill the vacuum. Deliver a clear message: Regional Auto Group has navigated every disruption in its history, we are assessing this one with clear eyes, and no decisions about staffing or structure will be made in panic. Frame the threat honestly but not catastrophically. The goal is to stop the bleeding of morale before it starts, not to pretend there is no wound.
past_actions.emotional_state: controlled alarm — the kind that sharpens rather than scatters

past_actions.summary: Request a private, off-calendar meeting with Angela Wright — not in her office, not at HQ. Invite her to lunch at a location off auto row. The agenda is not 'I know you're talking to an attorney.' The agenda is: I want her to tell me, in her own words, what she is seeing in the organization and what she thinks we should be doing. Give her the conversational opening to be honest about her own position without forcing her to disclose. Make clear that her role in a restructuring scenario — if there is one — is not to be eliminated, it is to be the architect of it. Offer to discuss formalizing her participation in the strategic planning process with a defined retention agreement: 90-day stay bonus of $12,000, contingent on her leading the workforce transition plan, whatever form that takes.
past_actions.emotional_state: Deliberate. The alarm is still there but it has shifted from sharp to cold. I am not scared of what I might find out anymore — I am scared of finding out too late. The hardest part of this tick is not the money decisions. It is admitting to the people who work for me that I am modeling a smaller future, and asking them to help me build it.

past_actions.summary: Issue Angela Wright her first formal deliverable as Director of Org Transition: a 30-day workforce vulnerability map. Every role at every location, categorized by three tiers — EV/AV-exposed (could be eliminated if service volume drops and we do not upskill), transition-ready (can be retrained or redeployed), and anchored (customer-facing or management roles with defensible value in any future model). This is not a layoff list. This is intelligence. I frame it to her exactly that way. I also confirm the $12,000 stay bonus is active and the clock is running.

Call Rick Tanner into a direct executive meeting — not a phone call, a sit-down in my office — and require him to present the 30-day sales and service data he has been quietly compiling. Make clear that information flow in this organization runs through me, not around me. Review unit volume, margin trends, and service lane health together. If the numbers are as bad as I suspect, begin drafting a formal Q2 operational plan with Rick that addresses the floor's reduced throughput honestly rather than hoping it recovers.
